newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour's Brown pledges no new spending plans.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour's Brown pledges no new spending plans.

text.p: The opposition Labour Party will promise later on Monday that it will make no spending commitments in advance of the British election other than those which can be financed by its planned windfall tax.
"I can confirm...that we will be making no new commitments in our manifesto which require additional spending," economics spokesman Gordon Brown will say in a keynote speech.

"Tony Blair and I have made clear that our programme requires no new spending commitments other than those financed by the windfall tax," Brown will say, according to an advance copy of his remarks received by the Press Association news agency.
Brown now expects to raise some 10 billion stg from the windfall tax, which will be levied on all utilities privatised by the Conservatives.
He will make his speech, billed as the first of a series setting out Labour's plans for the economy, at 1445 gmt in London.
